paper_title: Increased conjugated backbone twisting to improve carbonylated-functionalized polymer photovoltaic performance

qa_pairs.question: What is the structural difference between the conjugated polymers PBTCO-TT and PBTCO-T?
qa_pairs.answer: PBTCO-TT and PBTCO-T are both based on benzo[1,2-b:4,5-b′]dithiophene (BDT) and carbonylated thiophene units. The only difference between them is the linker used between the two carbonylated thiophene units: PBTCO-TT utilizes a thieno[3,2-b]thiophene (TT) linker, while PBTCO-T utilizes a thiophene (T) linker.
qa_pairs.source_title: Increased conjugated backbone twisting to improve carbonylated-functionalized polymer photovoltaic performance

qa_pairs.question: What are the photovoltaic performance parameters (PCE, Voc, Jsc, and FF) for the PBTCO-T:ITIC-based solar cell?
qa_pairs.answer: The PBTCO-T:ITIC-based polymer solar cell achieved a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 10.40%. The open-circuit voltage (Voc) was 0.959 V, the short-circuit current density (Jsc) was 16.21 mA cm⁻², and the fill factor (FF) was 66.89%.
qa_pairs.source_title: Increased conjugated backbone twisting to improve carbonylated-functionalized polymer photovoltaic performance

qa_pairs.question: How does the choice of linker (T vs TT) between carbonylated thiophene units influence the conjugated backbone twist angles in PBTCO-T and PBTCO-TT?
qa_pairs.answer: According to DFT calculations at the B3LYP/6-31g (d, p) level, replacing the thieno[3,2-b]thiophene (TT) unit with a thiophene (T) unit increases the twist angles of the polymer backbone. Specifically, PBTCO-T trimers exhibit twist angles up to 34.3°, whereas PBTCO-TT trimers show lower twist angles of up to 25.6°.
qa_pairs.source_title: Increased conjugated backbone twisting to improve carbonylated-functionalized polymer photovoltaic performance

qa_pairs.question: Why does PBTCO-T form a better bulk heterojunction morphology with ITIC compared to PBTCO-TT?
qa_pairs.answer: The increased twist angles in the PBTCO-T conjugated backbone result in weaker aggregation in solution compared to PBTCO-TT. This suppressed aggregation prevents the formation of excessive large-scale clusters, leading to a more optimized bulk heterojunction (BHJ) morphology and a significantly smoother film surface (RMS roughness of 1.51 nm for PBTCO-T vs 9.06 nm for PBTCO-TT).
qa_pairs.source_title: Increased conjugated backbone twisting to improve carbonylated-functionalized polymer photovoltaic performance

qa_pairs.question: Compare the charge carrier mobilities and transport balance of PBTCO-T:ITIC and PBTCO-TT:ITIC blend films.
qa_pairs.answer: PBTCO-T:ITIC blend films exhibit significantly higher and more balanced charge transport than PBTCO-TT:ITIC. PBTCO-T:ITIC has a hole mobility (μh) of 1.15 × 10⁻⁴ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ and an electron mobility (μe) of 3.78 × 10⁻⁴ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ (ratio of 3.3), while PBTCO-TT:ITIC shows a much lower μh of 2.11 × 10⁻⁶ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ and a highly imbalanced μe/μh ratio of 93.4.
qa_pairs.source_title: Increased conjugated backbone twisting to improve carbonylated-functionalized polymer photovoltaic performance

qa_pairs.question: Based on temperature-dependent UV-Vis absorption, how do the aggregation tendencies of PBTCO-TT and PBTCO-T compare in chlorobenzene?
qa_pairs.answer: PBTCO-TT has a stronger aggregation tendency than PBTCO-T. Temperature-dependent UV-Vis absorption spectra in chlorobenzene show that PBTCO-TT maintains its aggregation even at 90 °C, whereas PBTCO-T does not show aggregation at that temperature.
qa_pairs.source_title: Increased conjugated backbone twisting to improve carbonylated-functionalized polymer photovoltaic performance

qa_pairs.question: How does the exciton dissociation probability (Pdiss) correlate with the short-circuit current density (Jsc) in PBTCO-T and PBTCO-TT based devices?
qa_pairs.answer: The PBTCO-T:ITIC-based device has a higher exciton dissociation probability (Pdiss) of 80.55% compared to 60.62% for the PBTCO-TT:ITIC-based device. This higher Pdiss in the PBTCO-T device directly contributes to its superior short-circuit current density (Jsc) of 16.21 mA cm⁻².
qa_pairs.source_title: Increased conjugated backbone twisting to improve carbonylated-functionalized polymer photovoltaic performance

qa_pairs.question: What differences are observed in the XRD diffraction patterns of PBTCO-TT:ITIC and PBTCO-T:ITIC blend films regarding molecular stacking?
qa_pairs.answer: XRD analysis reveals that PBTCO-T:ITIC blend films possess a strong π-π diffraction peak at 24.12° (0.37 nm), indicating good crystallinity and stacking. In contrast, PBTCO-TT:ITIC blend films show a strong chain-to-chain peak at 4.63° but an extremely weak π-π stacking peak, suggesting a different and less favorable molecular arrangement for charge transport.
qa_pairs.source_title: Increased conjugated backbone twisting to improve carbonylated-functionalized polymer photovoltaic performance
